summary: In San Jose, installing or replacing any water heater needs a plumbing permit; heat pump models also need an electrical permit, and other electric models need one for new electrical work.

outcomes.explanation: A heat pump water heater needs both a plumbing permit and an electrical permit. For a single-family home or duplex you can get them online at SJPermits.org.

An electric water heater needs a plumbing permit, and an electrical permit for any new electrical work such as a new circuit. For a single-family home or duplex you can apply for both online in one session.

default_explanation: Installing or replacing a water heater needs a plumbing permit in San Jose. San Jose's plumbing exemptions cover only stopping leaks, clearing stoppages, and repairs that do not replace or rearrange valves, pipes, or fixtures.
permit_types: Electrical permit (heat pump models, or any new electrical work)
fee_note: San Jose's FY 2025-26 fee schedule bills plumbing permit inspection at a minimum of $315 per hour, with a 30-minute default minimum per item, in addition to the permit issuance fee. For a water heater replacement pulled through Online Permits, the minimum permit issuance fee is $0.
inspections: Inspection after the water heater is installed

notes.text: Single-family homes and duplexes can get the permit online at SJPermits.org. If the property does not qualify, the city's Standard Plan Review Service applies.
On the plan review path, an electric water heater application must include electrical load calculations showing the existing service is adequate.
Schedule an inspection after the water heater is installed.
Every new or replacement water heater, and every existing residential water heater, must be braced, anchored, or strapped against earthquake motion.
Fees: plumbing inspection is a minimum of $315 per hour with a 30-minute default minimum per item, plus a permit issuance fee; water heater replacements pulled online have a $0 minimum issuance fee.

Online permits can be pulled only by the property owner or a qualified contractor. The city recommends that a licensed contractor pull the permit; an owner-builder must also submit the Owner Acknowledgement and Information Verification Form, show ID at issuance, and be the owner of record.
San Jose adopted the 2025 California Plumbing Code; the 2025 codes apply to permit applications made on or after January 1, 2026.
With the 2025 code adoption, San Jose repealed its earlier local reach code amendments to the Energy Code and green building code.
A July 2025 city staff memo says Bay Area Air District rules will require new water heaters to meet a zero-NOx standard in phases beginning in 2027. Confirm the dates with the Air District.

citations.code_section: San Jose Permit Center, Water Heaters (updated 04/14/2026), Tankless Water Heaters
citations.quote: All new electrical work requires an electrical permit. For single-family/duplex projects, the plumbing and electrical permits can be applied for in one session at SJPermits.org.

A plumbing permit shall not be required for the following: A. The stopping of leaks in drains, soil, waste or vent pipe, provided, however, that should any concealed trap, drainpipe, soil, waste or vent pipe become defective and it becomes necessary to remove and replace the same with new material, such work shall be considered as new work and a permit shall be obtained and inspection made as provided in this title. B. The clearing of stoppages or the repairing of leaks in pipes, valves or fixtures, and the removal and reinstallation of water closets, provided such repairs do not involve or require the replacement or rearrangement of valves, pipes or fixtures. C. Reserved.

citations.code_section: San Jose Permit Center, Water Heaters (updated 04/14/2026), Strapping & Bracing
citations.quote: The California Plumbing Code mandates that all types of water heaters are required to be braced and strapped to resist moving or tipping during an earthquake. This applies to new and replacement water heaters and existing water heaters.

citations.code_section: Cal. Health & Safety Code §19211(a)
citations.quote: Notwithstanding Section 19100, all new and replacement water heaters, and all existing residential water heaters, shall be braced, anchored, or strapped to resist falling or horizontal displacement due to earthquake motion. At a minimum, any water heater shall be secured in accordance with the California Plumbing Code, or modifications made thereto by a city, county, or city and county pursuant to Section 17958.5.

research_notes: Access: every live sanjoseca.gov URL tried, robots.txt included, returned HTTP 403 'Access Denied' (Akamai) to curl and to WebFetch. City pages were read from raw Internet Archive captures (id_ mode, fetched with curl, tags stripped with python3, the fee schedule PDF read with pdftotext). source_url is the capture URL; the official sanjoseca.gov URL is the part after the timestamp. The captured robots.txt (https://web.archive.org/web/20260501010517/https://www.sanjoseca.gov/robots.txt) disallows only /scripts, /admin and *.asmx for all agents. The city's E-Government Policy (sanjoseca.gov/home/showdocument?id=17869, capture 20260904222013) has no rule against copying or automated access. Internet Archive terms say access 'is granted for scholarship and research purposes only'. Re-check each city quote on the live page before marking a rule verified. Quote format: list items and paragraph breaks are joined with single spaces and bullet characters are left out; ' ... ' marks omitted text; the words are verbatim. sjpermits.org robots.txt is 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /', so the SJPermits portal was not fetched; online-permit availability comes from the city's Online Building Permits page. Municode (host of the San Jose Municipal Code) was not fetched. Its archived terms (https://web.archive.org/web/20190411032708/https://www.municode.com/terms-of-use/) say: 'You may not copy, modify, reproduce, republish, distribute, display, or transmit for commercial, non-profit or public purposes all or any portion of this Website, except to the extent permitted by these Terms and Conditions of Use.' The current terms page could not be loaded. SJMC text: quotes marked 'Ord. No. 31256' come from the council-agenda redline of that ordinance (draft dated 10/16/2025, Council Agenda 10/28/2025 Item 8.2(a), file 25-1131), downloaded through the Legistar Web API (webapi.legistar.com); sanjose.granicus.com robots.txt has 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /'. Each such quote is the enacted wording: struck-through text removed and underlined additions kept, checked against the rendered PDF page. Legistar matter 25-1187 (Final Adoption of Ordinances, dated 2025-10-30) lists 'Ordinance No. 31256' as passed for publication on 10/28/2025; the signed ordinance and the final vote were not retrieved. Code edition: San Jose adopted the 2025 California codes (not 2022) for permit applications made on or after January 1, 2026. SJMC 24.09.110(A)(6) does not adopt CRC Chapter 1, Division II, so CRC §R105.2 does not apply in San Jose; the city's exemption lists are SJMC 24.02.120 to 24.02.150. Section numbering: the When Is a Building Permit Required? page (updated 06/12/2025) cites 'Section 24.02.110' for the exempt list, but Ord. No. 31256 amends the exemption lists as 24.02.120 (building), 24.02.130 (plumbing), 24.02.140 (mechanical) and 24.02.150 (electrical). Fees: the fee schedule capture is the FY 2025-26 schedule ('Effective August 11, 2025', document 26047 version 637922894017900000, captured 2025-12-07). The Building Permit Fees page captured 2026-08-01 still says the schedule shows fees in effect as of August 11, 2025, but links a newer upload (version 639180865996470000) with no capture, so the current PDF could not be compared. A draft FY 2026-27 fee resolution (Council Agenda 06-09-2026 Item 3.4(b), Legistar file 26-683) sets different amounts ('Water Heater Replacement – Permit Center 0.25 x # of units $52'); its adoption was not confirmed, so it is not cited. Reach codes: Ord. No. 31257 (Council Agenda 10/28/2025 Item 8.2(b)) repealed SJMC 24.10 Parts 2 and 3 and 24.12 Parts 2 through 8, the city's earlier local green building and Energy Code amendments. A proposed Existing Single-Family Building Reach Code (Legistar files 25-803 and 25-942) would have required a heat pump when an air conditioner is replaced or added, and electric-ready wiring near gas appliances. An unofficial meeting summary (citizenportal.ai) reports 'The motion failed after a 5–4 recorded vote and did not take effect.' It is not cited, and its adoption status was not confirmed from an official record. The July 21, 2025 staff memo (file 25-803) says AB 130 prohibits new residential building standards, including reach codes, 'from October 1, 2025, through June 1, 2031.' Inferred, not quoted: no San Jose rule found requires a heat pump or all-electric replacement in an existing home. Params: like_for_like does not change the verdict for a single-family home or duplex. The Water Heaters page uses like-for-like only for its multifamily and commercial online path, which this record does not model. Electric water heaters: the page says an electrical permit 'may also be required' depending on the type and that 'All new electrical work requires an electrical permit'. It does not say whether a plug-for-plug electric replacement on an existing circuit needs one, so the electric outcome ties the electrical permit to new electrical work. Fee quote fee_wh comes from the Special and Miscellaneous Fees section; whether it also applies to the plumbing sub-trade issuance fee was not confirmed. docs_required is empty because the city lists documents only for the Standard Plan Review path.
